findings.title: Seal binds working tree, not HEAD — in-version repair escape
findings.detail: validate_artifact_seal compares `git show <seal>:<path>` to artifact_path.read_bytes() and never to HEAD:<path>, with no clean-tree check. A repair committed after the seal passes whenever the working tree is reverted (e.g. `git checkout <seal> -- <path>`), so the audit certifies bytes that differ from the committed artifact. The same working-tree assumption underlies every checked_file reference (blindDerivationRef, comparisonRef, revealedArtifacts), breaking the bytes/ancestry binding chain.

findings.title: Target and semantic hash pins are shadowable via mapping union
findings.detail: manifest_sources is a last-wins union of all reveal_hashes mappings; downstream-target and semantic-projection sha256 values are checked only against that union, never against frozenSemanticHashes or a dedicated target pin. A colliding path in any other mapping overrides the frozen pin, so the target or a semantic projection can be certified with bytes that differ from the frozen corpus.

findings.title: 'All comparison commits before adjudication' is caller-trusted, not enforced
findings.detail: required_comparison_commits is an externally supplied tuple: nothing verifies it contains every comparison seal commit, or even the commit of the comparison named by comparisonRef, and comparisons whose seal derivation returns None drop out of the set. An empty or partial tuple silently disables the gate; nothing here detects multiple comparison files per unit or requires the result to adjudicate the latest one.

findings.title: Fail-open skips plus crash on unhashable IDs
findings.detail: Non-dict entries in revealedArtifacts, discrepancies and verificationReviews are `continue`d with no failure recorded, so required target/semantic reveals, discrepancy verification and reviewer-independence rules can be evaded by hiding entries as non-object JSON unless the schema hard-enforces object items. Conversely, unhashable reviewId/discrepancyId values raise TypeError and crash the validator instead of appending a failure.

findings.title: Unknown severity falls through to 'accepted'
findings.detail: validate_result's terminal else demands status 'accepted' for any severity outside {critical, material, blocked}; unless the comparison schema hard-enums severity, a novel or misspelled value adjudicates a real discrepancy as clean. 'blocked' rows are also exempt from the rootCauseId requirement imposed on material/critical.

residual_risks: Ancestry/confinement semantics live in unseen helpers: if require_preseal_after_all is weaker than merge-base --is-ancestor, or checked_file's default base admits absolute or '..' paths (revealed-artifact calls pass no base dir), ordering and path bindings are weaker than assumed.
sealedAtUtc ordering is self-attested wall-clock, not Git committer dates.
__-prefixed enrichments (__packetSourceHashes, __packetEvidenceIds, __completenessReviewerIdentity) are trusted in-memory and not re-verified against disk here.
The seal commit may bundle unrelated changes; no check that it touches only the sealed path.
Comparator prompt is pinned at the response's seal commit (prompt_commit=comparison_commit), not at the blind's seal commit.
Empty semantic-ID declarations pass, duplicate IDs within one id_field are not rejected, and there is no TOCTOU guard against mutation during the validation run.
